name: hostnamectl
description: systemd's control tool for the hostname plus a summary of the OS, kernel, and virtualization.

flags.description: Show hostname, OS, kernel, architecture, and virtualization.
Set a display name (spaces allowed) alongside the static name.

examples.output:
Static hostname: webserver01
       Icon name: computer-vm
 Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS
           Kernel: Linux 6.8.0-45-generic
     Architecture: x86-64
   Virtualization: kvm
examples.explanation: A one-stop summary: OS release, kernel, architecture, and that this is a KVM virtual machine.
Permanently renames the machine — updates /etc/hostname and the running kernel immediately. Also update /etc/hosts if it references the old name.

about: hostnamectl talks to systemd-hostated over D-Bus. It reports the distro from /etc/os-release and detects the hypervisor (kvm, vmware, microsoft, docker). It is the correct tool for hostname changes on any systemd distribution.
useCases: Identify OS and virtualization at a glance.
mistakes: Editing /etc/hostname manually and forgetting to apply it — hostnamectl does both.
distroNotes: systemd distributions only (all major Linux distros today).
